full_judgment:
Mr. Syed Md. Ziaul Karim .J:- Plaintiff petitioner on presentation of a petition under Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure(briefly as Code) seeks Review of a judgment dated 28-02-2007, recorded by this Court in Civil Revision no.5049 of 2004, discharging the Rule arising out of the judgment and order dated 09-11-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Pabna. in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 18 of 2004, affirming those of dated 25-04-2004 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Pabna, in Other Class Suit No. 72 of 2003; rejecting an application for temporary injunction. 

 4. On 27-10-2003 the petitioner as plaintiff instituted. Other Class Suit No. 72 of 2003, in the Court of Assistant Judge, Pabna, impleading the opposite parties as defendants for declaration that the letter dated 18-10-2003 issued under the signature of Chairman of the Governing body of Md. Yeasin Degree College (Opposite party No.1) suspending the petitioner from the post of Assistant Professor Psychology Department is illegal, without jurisdiction, void and not binding upon the petitioner. On, the some date the plaintiff also filed an application under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 of the Code for temporary injunction for restraining the defendants. 

 6. Plaintiff petitioner felt dissatisfied of the above adjudication of the matter and invoked this Court's Revisional Jurisdiction under section 115 of The Code on presentation of Revision Petition and obtained Rule. Revision Petition had been numbered as Civil Revision no. 5049 of 2004. After hearing, this Court by the judgment and order dated 28-02-2007 discharged the Rule on the following grounds: - 

 "On consideration of the materials on record, I find that the order of suspension was for temporary period and the final order was not passed. Therefore 1 hold that the application for temporary injunction was pre-mature. Both the Courts below concurrently held that the plaintiff has no prima facie case and the application for temporary injunction was pre-mature. I do not find any reason to differ with such concurrent views." 

 "In the instant case, the plaintiff failed to show any one of the aforesaid principles: Moreover, the trial Court directed to the concerned authority of the College to. pay 50% of the Government allowance to the plaintiff. It further appeais that the Courts below concurrently held that the plaintiff will not suffer any irreparable loss or injury by the impugned decision of the College. Moreover, no final order has Yet been passed against the plaintiff I am also in agreement with the aforesaid concurrent views of the Courts below." 

 8. The learned Counsel also refers the case of Bijoy Kumar Shaha Vs. DC, Chuadanga and others, reported in 55 DLR-550 wherein it is held: "Suspension of an employee pending a disciplinary proceeding is an approved measure and the Court does not generally interfere with it. But if the order of suspension is prima facie illegal and tinged with malafide, the Court is competent to act for preventing  injustice. 

 9. The learned Counsel lastly submits that in view of the aforesaid facts the petitioner established a prima-facie case for obtaining an order of temporary injunction and as such the judgment and order dated 28-02-2007 passed by this Court may be reviewed. 

 "Three well-established principles of km governing the grant of temporary injunction are the following: First, the plaintiff' has to establish a prima facie case. Secondly, it was to he shown that the plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss if the injunction prayed for is not granted and thirdly, the balance of convenience lies in favour of the plaintiff and in favour of granting the temporary injunction prayed for. 

 In the instant case, the plaintiff failed to show any one of the aforesaid principles and as such she is not entitled to get an order of temporary injunction.
